instruction_summary: Re-estimate ADH (2013) 'China Syndrome' four headline 2SLS claims on post-2007 windows (2007-12, 2012-19, 2019-24) across 722 CZs and visualize how the China-shock coefficients evolved from the 1990-2007 sample to today.

steps.description: Rebuilt venv from replication package list; read replication artifacts (iv.py helper, workfile, ADH headline CSVs)
steps.command: uv venv /workspace/.venv && uv pip install pandas numpy scipy linearmodels statsmodels matplotlib openpyxl xlrd requests pyarrow

steps.description: Downloaded crosswalks, cbp_czone_merged, china9114, ADH Persistence archive, CEPII BACI HS92 V202601 (2.4GB)
steps.command: curl ddorn.net + cepii.fr BACI zip; stream-filter China->9 importers for 2007/12/19/24

steps.description: Built ΔIPW exposure (US + instrument) per CZ for W3-W5 from BACI+cbp weights, deflated to 2007$; validated vs workfile (r=0.95), Persistence (r=0.855), china9114 (r=0.90-0.95)
Built C1 outcome: CBP mfg jobs (31----) / popest working-age pop by CZ, 2000-2023, with CT planning-region fix
Built C4 outcome: BEA CAINC35 transfers per capita (2007$), Δ$ and Δlog
Built C2 outcome: FRED LAUS county unemployment+labor force (3105 counties, checkpointed) -> CZ unemp/pop and NILF proxy
Built C3 outcome: QCEW county avg weekly wage -> CZ emp-weighted Δlog wage
Ran per-window 2SLS (primary + frozen-full), W1/W2 original anchors, and pooled window-interaction model; first-stage F per window
Produced flagship 4-panel figure with national-context strip and compact card figure

key_results.all_claims_W4_W5: C2/C3/C4 all fade to statistically insignificant near-zero in 2012-2019 and 2019-2024
key_results.exposure_validation: r=0.954 vs original workfile; r=0.855 vs ADH Persistence p1; r=0.90-0.95 BACI vs china9114

comparison_to_original.note: Effect essentially unchanged from ADH era through 2012 while shock active, then fades to zero and reverses as shock plateaus/reverses.
W2 proxy closely reproduces ADH, validating the LAUS proxy; effect gone after 2007.

comparison_to_original.quantity: C3 log weekly wage coefficient (log pts)
comparison_to_original.note: Same sign, fades to zero by 2012-19.

comparison_to_original.quantity: C4 log transfers per capita coefficient (log pts)
comparison_to_original.note: Persists into W3, then fades; most persistent of the four claims.

deviations: W4 (2012-2019) 2SLS is weakly identified (first-stage F=6.9<10); flagged on figure, corroborated by reduced form and pooled model.

Outcomes are jobs/BEA-based proxies (CBP mfg jobs; LAUS 16+ labor force with 15-64 denominator; QCEW jobs-based nominal wage; BEA total transfers, SSDI not separable) rather than ADH's Census/ACS person-level measures (IPUMS unavailable); levels differ but window changes consistent, and W2 proxy reproduces the original outcomes.
W5 employment weights frozen at 2011 (2019 CBP NAICS2017->SIC87 chain too lossy; sanctioned by failure playbook and ADH's BPEA follow-up).
C4 W5 window is 2019-2022 (BEA CAINC35 vintage ends 2022, confirmed no fresher release); scaled 10/3. C1/C2/C3 W5 outcome 2019-2023 scaled 10/4.
BACI used for all new windows (W3-W5) for one internally-consistent trade source instead of mixing in china9114 for W3 (china9114 retained as validation anchor).
Switzerland corrected to BACI numeric code 757 (instruction said 756; verified against country_codes_V202601.csv).
Connecticut adopted planning-region FIPS in 2022; all CT counties belong to CZ 20901, so CT is routed there for 2023 CBP/LAUS/popest files.
